newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Supreme Court upholds Bhutto dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Supreme Court upholds Bhutto dismissal.

text.p: Pakistan's Supreme Court announced on Wednesday it had upheld President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
The keenly-awaited judgement, by a 6-1 majority of the seven-judge bench, means Monday's national and provincial elections will go ahead as planned.
"We uphold the order of the president and dismiss the petition" Bhutto brought, Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah said in court.
President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government on November 5, accusing it of corruption and misrule, charges Bhutto denies. Fresh elections are set for February 3.

Shah said the court dismissed Bhutto's petition because it agreed with Leghari's charges of corruption, extra-judicial killings, delay in separating the judiciary from the executive and humililation of the judiciary.
